headline: AI rout and a hawkish BoJ hold pull yields lower; soft German CPI keeps the dollar flat
summary: The dollar index ended roughly flat near 101.9 after dipping to about 101.7: Intel and Amazon deepened the AI selloff and pushed Treasury yields lower, but the euro slid from 1.12 after softer German inflation. The Singapore dollar, loonie and yen led on falling US yields, $117 oil and a hawkish BoJ, while the euro (−0.2%) lagged and Taiwan's dollar needed the central bank as foreigners dumped shares.
drivers: AI cash burn hits stocks, lifts bonds

Intel fell 28.6% and Amazon's $42bn cash outflow revived AI-spending fears; the Nasdaq dropped 2.9%, its worst day since June 5. The 10-year yield fell about 5bp to near 4.93% and the 2-year about 5bp to 4.60%, which pulled the dollar to about 101.7 before the euro's slide.
BoJ holds at 1.25% but leans hawkish

The vote was 8–1 with Takata seeking 1.5%, the FY2027 inflation forecast rose to 2.6%, ETF sales nearly triple from January, and Ueda said December is live. The yen hit about 157.0, then gave back most of it to close near 157.57.

Brent rose about 2.4% to near $117.6, its highest since April, on reports of US strike options against Iran, lifting the loonie to a six-week high despite flat August GDP. Sterling touched 1.3429 on a near-certain BoE hike, while German CPI falling to 2.8% knocked the euro to 1.1137.
view: Neutral with a mild softening bias over the next 1–2 weeks: AI-driven bond buying keeps yields falling, and the dollar no longer gains on strong data because a December Fed hike is priced. I fade the dollar against the yen, loonie and ringgit, where central banks are hiking or about to, but still back it against the euro and rupiah. A DXY close above 102.80 would make me dollar-positive; below 101.70 I would turn outright bearish.
ideas: Short from 157.50–157.80 (filled) as the BoJ keeps December live and Tokyo guards 160; for 155.00, stop 158.60.
Short from 1.4030–1.4050, about 0.5% in favour on oil and BoC hikes; for 1.3850, stop lowered to 1.4040.
Sell 4.055–4.065, a lower zone after missing the last, before Bank Negara on Nov 5; for 4.010, stop 4.085.
review: USD/CAD's short is about 0.5% in favour, EUR/USD's about 0.2% after the euro faded from 1.12, and USD/KRW, EUR/JPY and USD/JPY 0.05–0.3%; USD/IDR's long is about 0.8% up and AUD/USD flat. USD/TWD's fade survived a spike to 32.676 as the central bank pulled the close to 32.478. The USD/CNH and ringgit sell zones were missed, so I lower both; all ranges held.

eurusd.note: Down 0.2% to 1.1158 after failing just above 1.1200; low 1.1137 on softer German CPI.
eurusd.why: The euro did the moving. It rose above 1.12 in Europe as US yields fell, then dropped when German inflation slowed to 2.8%, mostly thanks to a fuel rebate, trimming bets on a December ECB hike. Italy's jump to 5.4% and Spain's 4.9% kept the region's inflation picture mixed, and Q3 growth of 0.4% still lags the US.
eurusd.outlook: Bearish: I hold the short from 1.1170–1.1190 for 1.1050, as slower euro-area growth and $117 oil weigh. I tighten the stop to 1.1220, above Friday's high; a close there, likely on a hot euro-area flash CPI, ends the call.
eurusd.watch: Euro-area flash CPI next week, French spreads, oil and US payrolls.

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; growth gap, oil weigh.

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.1% to 1.3387 after touching 1.3429; up about 1% in October.
gbpusd.why: Sterling did most of the moving. With the budget out of the way, traders almost fully price a BoE hike on Nov 5 and a second by February, which made the pound the best major early on Friday. It gave back most of the gain as the dollar steadied late, but EUR/GBP stayed near a 17-month low around 0.835.
gbpusd.outlook: Range 1.3280–1.3450, upper half: I buy dips near 1.3300 while BoE hike pricing holds. A close above 1.3450 after a hawkish Nov 5 turns me bullish; below 1.3280 bearish.
gbpusd.watch: The BoE (Nov 5), UK data and US payrolls.

view.call: 1.3280–1.3450; buy dips, BoE Nov 5 is the swing.

audusd.note: Flat at 0.7031, holding above 0.7000 despite the global tech selloff.
audusd.why: Two forces cancelled out. The Nasdaq's 2.9% fall weighed on the risk-sensitive Aussie, but lower US yields and firm commodity prices offset it. Markets still price about 85% odds that the RBA lifts its rate to 4.85% on Tuesday after hot third-quarter inflation.
audusd.outlook: I hold the long from 0.7020–0.7035 for 0.7130: an RBA hike widens the rate gap with the Fed. A close below 0.6970, likely on an RBA hold or a deeper equity rout, ends the call.
audusd.watch: China PMIs (Oct 31), the RBA (Nov 3) and US tech stocks.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.1% to 157.57 after a post-BoJ low near 157.0; a third daily yen gain.
usdjpy.why: Both sides moved. The BoJ held at 1.25% but one member voted to hike, it raised its FY2027 inflation forecast to 2.6% and said it will sell ETFs faster, while Ueda kept December live. Falling US yields added pressure, but the yen gave back most of its jump as traders had expected the hawkish tone.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the short from 157.50–157.80 for 155.00: about 80% December BoJ odds, lower US yields and Tokyo's guard near 159–160 cap the pair. A close above 158.60 ends the call.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo intervention talk, US yields, US payrolls and BoJ speakers.

view.call: Short from 157.50–157.80; BoJ eyes Dec, Tokyo warns.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.1% to 0.8250, mid-range, as the franc paused after Thursday's jump.
usdchf.why: The dollar side moved slightly. The franc had rallied hard on Thursday's haven buying, and Friday's tech rout sent more money into Treasuries and the yen than the franc. The euro's late slide also dragged on the franc through EUR/CHF.
usdchf.outlook: Range 0.8200–0.8300. A close below 0.8200, the Oct 22 low, would open 0.8150; calm in tech stocks would pull it back toward 0.8300.
usdchf.watch: Swiss CPI (early Nov), US tech stocks and risk sentiment.

usdcad.note: Down about 0.14% to 1.3970 after a six-week low of 1.3943; loonie up about 2% in October.
usdcad.why: The loonie did the moving. Brent jumped about 2.4% toward $117.6 on US strike options against Iran, and that supported bets the Bank of Canada will keep hiking. Traders ignored a stall in August GDP and a likely 0.1% dip in September, which left Q3 growth at 1.3% against the BoC's 2%.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the short from 1.4030–1.4050, about 0.5% in favour, for 1.3850, and lower the stop to 1.4040: oil and the BoC–Fed gap favour the loonie. A close above 1.4040, likely on an oil slump or tariff news, ends the call.
usdcad.watch: Oil and Iran, US tariff headlines, Canada jobs and US payrolls.

usdcnh.note: Down about 0.06% to near 6.653; the yuan is heading for a fourth monthly gain.
usdcnh.why: The yuan kept edging up, but at Beijing's pace. The PBOC set its midpoint at 6.7138, its strongest since February 2023 yet 590 pips weaker than estimates, a second large weak-side gap in two days. The Fifth Plenum brought no new stimulus, and analysts read that as comfort with a slow, steady rise.
usdcnh.outlook: Managed grind lower: I sell 6.650–6.660, lower after the last zone was not reached, for 6.615. A close above 6.675 or a sharp China stock selloff ends the call.
usdcnh.watch: China PMIs (Oct 31), daily fixings vs estimates and US–China headlines.

view.call: Sell 6.650–6.660; PBOC allows a slow grind up.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.844, still close to the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Rate gaps keep it there. The HKMA held its base rate at 4.25% after the Fed, but Hong Kong interbank rates remain below US rates, so borrowing Hong Kong dollars to hold US dollars still pays. The pair stayed short of 7.85, so the HKMA had no need to act.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in the 7.83–7.85 band. A test of 7.85 would force HKMA buying and lift HIBOR; lower US yields would pull it off the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: HIBOR, HKMA action at 7.85 and US yields.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Down about 0.18% to near 1.2776, testing 50-day support around 1.2760.
usdsgd.why: The broad dollar did the moving. Lower US yields and a firmer yuan pulled the pair down, while the MAS's appreciating policy band keeps the Singapore dollar strong against its basket. Import prices rose 19.9% a year in September on energy, which keeps the MAS from softening its stance.
usdsgd.outlook: Range 1.2720–1.2830, now in the lower half; banks see support at 1.2760 and 1.2740. A close below 1.2720 reopens downside; above 1.2835 opens 1.2855–1.2900.
usdsgd.watch: The yuan, Singapore data, oil and US payrolls.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 2.5 to 1,334.3 at the Seoul close despite a 3.5% Kospi plunge.
usdkrw.why: Month-end flows did the moving. Exporters sold dollars into the month end and officials signalled readiness to steady the market, which reversed an early rise to 1,340.5. That outweighed custody-linked dollar buying as foreigners sold about 1.62 trillion won of shares and the Kospi fell 3.48% to 5,730.74.
usdkrw.outlook: I hold the short from 1,335–1,342 for 1,320, about 0.3% in favour, and tighten the stop to 1,343, above Friday's high. A close there on heavier foreign equity selling ends the call.
usdkrw.watch: Korea's October exports (Nov 1), CPI, foreign equity flows and US tech.

usdtwd.note: Onshore close 32.478, 1.4 cents firmer after a 32.676 low; down 1.9% in October.
usdtwd.why: Taiwan's equity flows and the central bank did the moving. The Taiex fell 1,156 points as foreigners sold about NT$112.5 billion of shares, pushing the Taiwan dollar to 32.676. The central bank then told big exporters to sell dollars and stepped in late, flipping the close to a small gain; October's loss was the largest in about ten years.
usdtwd.outlook: I hold the fade from 32.53 for 32.05: the central bank is clearly capping weakness and exporters hold large unsold dollars. A close above 32.65 on further foreign selling ends the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, US tech stocks, central bank action near 32.50–32.70.

view.call: Fade from 32.53; central bank caps, exporters sell.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit firmed to 4.0555/0600 at the 6pm close after hitting 4.0460, a near two-month high.
usdmyr.why: A softer dollar did most of the moving. The ringgit rose as traders trimmed Fed hike bets and the dollar index dipped toward 101.7, then gave back part of the gain as the dollar steadied. Malaysia's oil exports cushion it as Brent sits near $117, and talk of a Bank Negara move next week adds support.
usdmyr.outlook: I lower my sell zone to 4.055–4.065 after missing the last one, for 4.010: Bank Negara normalisation and oil favour the ringgit. A close above 4.085, likely if Bank Negara sounds dovish on Nov 5, ends the call.
usdmyr.watch: Bank Negara (Nov 5), oil and the yuan.

usdphp.note: Peso firmed 11 centavos to 63.74 at the BAP close, a third gain; down 1.8% in October.
usdphp.why: Official resolve and remittances helped. The BSP repeated that it is ready to intervene against excess volatility after President Marcos vowed to defend the peso, and dollar conversions of overseas workers' remittances before the Undas long weekend added support. Brent near $117 still caps gains, as fuel is a big import bill.
usdphp.outlook: Range 63.50–64.20: Manila's pledge caps the topside while oil and the external gap block a big rally. A close above 64.20 would restart the uptrend; below 63.50 opens 63.20.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments, oil and Iran, US midterms (Nov 3).

usdidr.note: Rupiah eased 10 points to 18,147 (Bloomberg) after a brief rally to about 18,100.
usdidr.why: Local pressure did the moving. The rupiah briefly firmed with Asia, then slipped as foreigners kept selling Jakarta stocks, oil climbed and protests across several cities added political risk. Bank Indonesia said fundamentals are fine relative to peers and it will keep the rupiah stable.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long, about 0.8% in favour, for 18,300: outflows, oil and politics keep pressure on. The intraday dip near 18,100 showed 18,110 was too tight, so I lower the stop to 18,060; a close there on heavy BI action ends the call.
usdidr.watch: Indonesia's October CPI, MSCI's review, Jakarta flows, BI action and oil.

usdinr.note: Rupee firmed about 33 paise to near 94.93 (provisional), its best close in over a week.
usdinr.why: A softer dollar and local stocks did the moving. Falling US yields and the Sensex's second daily gain helped the rupee rise from a 95.28 early low despite Brent near $115–117. Likely RBI dollar sales earlier in the week kept the pair from testing 95.50.
usdinr.outlook: Range 94.50–95.50: the RBI defends the top while oil above $110 blocks a big rally. A close above 95.50 would signal a new weaker leg; US strikes on Iran are the main risk.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran, RBI action and foreign flows.

view.call: 94.50–95.50; RBI near the top, oil caps the rupee.

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.3% to near 175.8 as the euro faded and the yen firmed after the BoJ.
eurjpy.why: Both legs moved the cross lower. The yen gained on the BoJ's hawkish hold and haven demand, while the euro slipped after German inflation came in softer than expected. That left the cross near 175.8 (EUR/USD 1.1158 × USD/JPY 157.57).
eurjpy.outlook: My short from 175.90–176.30 is about 0.15% in favour; I hold for 174.00 as the BoJ keeps December live and euro growth lags. A close above 177.00 ends the call.
eurjpy.watch: Euro-area flash CPI, BoJ speakers and risk sentiment.

view.call: Short from 175.90–176.30; BoJ hawkish, euro soft.

cnhjpy.note: Little changed near 23.68 as yuan and yen both firmed slightly.
cnhjpy.why: The legs offset. USD/CNH fell about 0.06% on a strong PBOC fixing and USD/JPY about 0.1% after the BoJ, leaving the cross near 23.68 (USD/JPY 157.57 ÷ USD/CNH 6.653), in the upper half of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range. A BoJ hike signal would push it toward 23.3; a break above 23.8 would need USD/JPY near 158.6.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, China PMIs (Oct 31) and BoJ speakers.

watch: Next: China PMIs (Oct 31), Korea exports (Nov 1), the RBA and US midterms (Nov 3), the BoE and Bank Negara (Nov 5), euro-area flash CPI and US payrolls, plus oil and Iran, US tech stocks and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
